1lxb184:176: The first landing point of token-level observability is slow-token identification. When a token's scheduling time is abnormally high (prefill preempts decode resources), at the Span level it appears as a sudden spike in that token's latency. Combined with batch load metrics, you can quickly determine whether it's resource interference under a PD-separated architecture or the model's own badcase. This is a direct way to locate BOS Token-type problems like off-topic answers.
1pgzinm:166: The implementation cost of gen_ai.skill.* attributes is extremely low—just attach four string attributes to the execute_tool Span, no new Span types needed. For systems with existing OTel instrumentation, this is a zero-breaking incremental capability. Platform side can do business-domain aggregation based on skill name and directly export Skill-level SLA / latency distributions without extra business instrumentation.
1tf01xl:173: Tool is an atomic operation (send_email, query_db), Agent is an autonomous decision unit, and Skill is the business-function aggregation point between the two. A Skill may call multiple Tools, but its semantics is a single business intent ("process refund", "verify qualification"). The gen_ai.skill.* attributes let observability data be aggregated by business domain rather than technical implementation, opening a direct path from observability to business analysis.

1v7qxeo:151: The data volume at per-token granularity is enormous—a 2048-token output generates 2048 data points. LoongSuite's approach: capture Top-K candidate distributions instead of full distributions, combine with batch load aggregation to reduce storage overhead, while retaining scheduling time as the key metric. This "downsample but don't lose key signals" approach is the crux of engineering feasibility.

3se9sd:213: If your framework doesn't yet support Entry/Step Span layering, consider introducing it once the number of Trace Spans exceeds 100. Entry Span records raw input/output (prompt/response), Step Span organizes by ReAct phase, and model calls, tool calls, and state transitions in each phase are mounted as child spans under the corresponding Step. This structure turns trace troubleshooting from O(N) linear scanning into O(log N) directory lookup.

v9r6kx:219: The traditional OTel HTTP Span model cannot map long-horizon AI Agent tasks. A single ReAct loop can span hundreds of internal calls—model inference, tool selection, memory recall—all compressed into one flat trace, making troubleshooting impossible. LoongSuite introduces Entry/Step layering: Entry Span anchors user intent at the Agent entry point, and Step Span expands parent-child relationships by ReAct phases, turning traces from a "tangled mess" into a "collapsible directory tree".
